reason: The transporter-bearing cell and arriving glucose and oxygen suggest the next step is getting fuel into the cell.
expectation: The cell will take in fuel for energy production.

effect: The cell first becomes a muscle fibre; the fuel and oxygen must be used elsewhere in the energy pathway.
reaction: The automatic pairing clarified the role of the cell, though my fuel guess was wrong.
reason: Thin actin and thick myosin filaments are the visible components of the muscle's pulling machinery.
expectation: They will form a contractile arrangement for the muscle fibre.

effect: The thin and thick filaments formed sliding filament units that can be added to the muscle fibre.
reaction: The overlapping arrangement makes their role in pulling clearer.
reason: The fibre has spaces for contractile units, so the sliding filaments appear ready to fit into it.
expectation: The sliding filament units will be installed in the muscle fibre.

effect: The filament units are now installed in the muscle fibre; it still needs energy and signals to pull and relax.
reaction: The construction makes the connection between the filaments and the whole fibre clear.
reason: Glucose and oxygen arrive at the cell, and mitochondria are associated with producing usable energy.
expectation: This will begin the energy-producing process needed by the muscle fibre.

effect: Glucose processing and oxygen supply have produced fuelled mitochondria, which appear ready to make ATP.
reaction: The picture clarifies that glucose is first split in the cell fluid.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the available ingredients for making ATP, and the mitochondria are now fuelled.
expectation: The fuelled mitochondria will produce ATP for the muscle fibre.

effect: The fuelled mitochondria produced an ATP supply, which can now support the fibre's pulling machinery.
reaction: The returning ADP and phosphate make ATP renewal clearer.
reason: The filament-filled fibre needs ATP to power its pulling machinery.
expectation: The ATP supply will equip the fibre for pulling.

effect: ATP has equipped the fibre, but the covered binding site suggests it still needs the calcium signal to pull.
reaction: The myosin close-up makes ATP's role in release and resetting clearer.
reason: The calcium signal reaches the fibre's filaments and may uncover their binding sites.
expectation: Calcium will enable the filaments to interact and the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites, allowing the filaments to slide and the fibre to shorten. The remaining calcium-pumping membranes suggest how it can relax.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments sliding is clear and interesting.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes can remove the calcium signal that enabled pulling.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage, allowing the fibre to relax.

effect: The calcium pumps returned calcium to storage using ATP, covering the grip sites and completing the fibre's pull-and-relax cycle.
reaction: It was interesting that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the calcium signal was most worthwhile: the description connects a cellular signal to filament movement and clearly distinguishes the fibre shortening from the filaments sliding.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the sliding filament units was straightforward but less revealing on its own; its main contribution was preparing the fibre for later steps.

surprise.text: I was struck that ATP helps myosin release and reset, and that pumps also use ATP during relaxation.

arbitrary.text: My first attempt to combine the cell with glucose and oxygen felt plausible from the titles, but the compatibility feedback showed that the cell first had to become a muscle fibre. The automatic pairing made the intended construction clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing the fibre assembled and then tracing how energy and calcium control its movement made me curious about how it contributes to a larger body system.
